spans.text: Bremen, Germany.
Flora Botanical Research Institute.
Guten Morgen, Frau Ange!
You look very well-rested.
Sorry for the wait.
Not at all, don't worry about me. It is my job to serve you.
Besides, I am very honored to be given the opportunity to learn from a woman as accomplished as you.
Oh, and from you too, Herr Hopps! Thank you for your work.
...Just doing my job.
He came to our place first thing in the morning.
That's Chairwoman Ulrich's trusted bodyguard for you!
Your personal safety is our top priority, Frau Ange.
Are you satisfied with your journey to this place?
It was alright, though it took Mr. Bodyguard a bit too long to shake off the car that was tailing us.
So, this is it?
That's right, this is the Flora Botanical Research Institute.
It is home to the largest botanical garden in Bremen, with seasonal flowers in bloom all year round.
If you're interested, I can give you a tour.
...Is that so?
I appreciate the gesture, but maybe next time.
Chairwoman Ulrich did say that your wish is my command.
But I never thought you'd be interested in botanical research!
Your sudden request for a visit really took me by surprise. Still, I do love flowers myself.
This is quite massive for a research institute.
Ja! The institute's research building is a famous landmark in Bremen.
They also have a large field on the other side of the city where they cultivate species for the purpose of research.
I see.
Come to think of it...
How come I don't see the Dolls that accompanied you to Bremen?
Is it a good idea for you to travel alone?
I'm just here for a visit; they'd just get in the way.
Besides, you've given me a personal bodyguard, isn't that right?
Absolutely!
Herr Hopps is such a reassuring presence!
It must be the beard!
...The beard?
To tell you the truth, this is also the first time I've ever been here.
What a beautiful greenhouse they have!
Who will we be meeting?
Uh, one second please. I believe we have an appointment with...
Oh, there she is!
Allow me to introduce...
Frau Leone, Senior Researcher at the Flora Botanical Research Institute.
She specializes in research on herbaceous plants.
...Hello.
Hello, I'm Angelia.
I know.
You're investigators sent by the Pan-European Convention on Mutual Assistance in Reconstruction, though I'm not sure what you're doing here.
As the one in charge, you're a lot younger than I imagined.
Such wonderful accomplishments for your age.
...You flatter me.
I'm just a humble researcher caring for my flowers.
We're sorry to bother you on a working day.
I hope we're not interrupting anything important?
Don't worry about it.
Help yourselves.
Huh? You're not going to show us around?
...I work in this greenhouse. If you have any questions, just ask.
I'm sorry, but I'm a researcher, not a tour guide.
Everyone have things they're good at and things they're...not so good at.
...I understand.
In...In that case, sorry to disturb you.
We don't seem very welcome here.
You're mistaken. You are Frau Ulrich's guests.
The Bremen government has been very supportive of our research.
It is my duty to fulfil her requests.
Then tell me more about yourself.
What kind of research do you do here?
...We mostly study the propagation and mutation of plants here at the Flora Institute.
In a world ravaged by mankind...
Plants are one of the few life forms that can resist radiation and survive.
We hope to find our "future" by studying them.
Find our "future"?
That doesn't sound like something a scientist would say. You didn't strike me as a hopeless romantic, Frau Leone.
Romantic?
I meant what I said literally; it was not a figure of speech.
Right now, mankind has no way of moving forward.
Yet plants have learned to live in harmony with despair long ago.
If we don't start learning from them, we may very well be sealing our fate.
Our future lies in plants?
What a peculiar idea.
Compared to humans, who never learn, plants that keep growing inconspicuously are much more reliable.
So what have you learned from these flowers?
...A great deal.
I've spoken more than I should.
Please take your time and have a look around.
Leone glances at her watch before heading to the other side of the greenhouse to check the thermometer.
Seriously? She came out to receive us, but she won't give us a tour?
Maybe Herr Hopps looks too intimidating?
I disagree.
S-Stop glaring at me.
I was just kidding.
Now that we're inside, the magnitude of their facility is even more apparent.
They're investing so much money and resources just to study flowers.
Is it worth it?
I don't think that's very fair, Frau Ange.
Under these times, everything we do must contribute to our survival.
But it's not the same for flowers.
Their fragrance and colors are only for embellishment; they aren't essential for the flowers' survival.
Of course, one must be pragmatic to survive, but virtues are equally—if not more—important.
What we can glean from flowers is hope.
That's a beautiful speech, but you did not answer my question.
J-Just sharing my thoughts!
This institute operates on such a large scale because it led the country's research in developing the vaccine and medication for ELID.
Their work has saved countless lives!
Right, Frau Leone?
...She's ignoring us altogether.
It feels as if she's keeping her distance deliberately, don't you think?
Now that you mention it, I'm getting the same feeling.
You're right, she does seem to be giving us a wide berth.
I knew it—she's unhappy that we're visiting out of the blue!
I wish it were that simple.
Um, I-I don't think Frau Leone is petty enough to be mad because of your little disagreement.
That's not what I meant.
It wasn't even a disagreement. I simply asked a couple of questions, but she didn't give any straight answers.
Ange takes in her surroundings.
I mean...
Other than us, this huge greenhouse is completely empty.
Don't you think that's odd?
Huh?
...It's too quiet.
Ms. Leone, eh?
A few steps away, Leone grows tense at Ange's question.
Where are the other researchers?
Surely you can't be the only one working in such a large institute.
Since we're having uninvited guests... I've sent everyone else home.
Uninvited guests, huh.
What a barbed way of putting it.
I didn't expect you to put the operation of your facility on hold for an entire day just because I'm here to visit. You're doing me too big a courtesy.
As I said, you are Chairwoman Ulrich's guests.
Not too subtle, are you?
Whoosh.
Ange draws her pistol and aims it straight at Leone.
The latter flinches visibly. Off to the side, Hopps also reaches for his weapon out of reflex.
Huh? What? H-Hold on a second? What are you doing?
Frau Ange?!
Tell me—where is everyone else?
Leone's lips twitch, but she does not utter a word.
Beep—
The tension in the air is broken by the sudden ring of Ange's communicator.
...What is it? What have you found?
Miss Ange, a large number of armed personnel is lying in ambush under the research facility.
Please get out immediately. This is a trap.
Got it.
Wow, serving the main course straight away? Not even bothering with some warm-up?
Wait... Huh? Ambush? A trap?
What even? J-Just what is going on?!
Hopps has his firearm trained on Leone in the blink of an eye.
Arms in the air!
Get down on the floor!
Humph...
With two guns pointed at her, the agitated Leone suddenly lets out a sneer.
The ending...has been decided since the moment you came in.
Just then, Ange hears a series of soft and rapid clicks coming from above her head.
Then the entire space is filled with pale yellow pollen.
What— P-Pollen?
A pungent scent assaults Ange's nose, giving her no time to react.
The world spins around her and her surroundings distort into something else.
...What?
What is this place...
How revolting...
Giving me the whole spiel about plants being the hope for humanity then leading me straight into a trap.
In the ruins, a few stumbling ELIDs emerge from around the corner and shuffle towards Ange.
I'm hallucinating... I've heard that certain pollens are hallucinogenic.
But I didn't expect the effect to be so potent... Maybe it's been processed?
None of this is real. Ange knows that very well.
Hallucinations... I know I'm just seeing things, but still.
Still...
She looks at the shambling ELIDs and takes a deep breath.
Don't blame me no matter what I hit.
She places her finger on the trigger and takes aim at the "ELIDs".
Just as she is about to pull the trigger...
A strong force dislodges the pistol from her hand.
Soon after that...
Her consciousness dissolves in chaos.
